_comment_howto: Single source of truth for all team members. Each member has a unique id (slug) used by member.html?id=<slug>. The 'role' field drives grouping on team.html — use exactly: 'Director', 'Co-Director', 'Researcher', 'Postdoctoral Researcher' (current postdocs), 'PhD Student', 'Master's Student', 'Undergraduate Student', 'Visiting Scholar', 'Alumni' (former students), 'Former Postdoc' (former postdocs). Set 'group' to 'national' or 'international' for collaborators. Photos go in assets/images/<id>.jpg (or .jpeg/.png) — leave 'photo' empty if you have no photo and a default monogram will be used. SUPPORTED FIELDS (all optional unless noted): id (required), name (required), honorific, credentials, role (required), subrole (e.g. 'PhD Alumni' for alumni), title, affiliation, email, photo, bibtex_name (the exact author-name string used for this person in publications.bib — when set, the publications page on their profile shows only their papers and bolds their name), research_topics (array), keywords (array of short tags), thesis (title), thesis_summary (short paragraph), degree (e.g. 'PhD in Industrial Engineering'), supervisors (array of member ids), bio_short, bio_long, education (array of strings), current_position, year (graduation year for alumni), start_year, expected_year, status, projects (array of project ids — optional manual override; usually filled automatically by matching project.team[].member_id to this id), links (object with any of: scholar, orcid, github, linkedin, website, anid, cv, twitter).

members.name: Felipe Feijoo
members.title: Associate Professor · Lab Director
members.bio_short: Director of the Energy & Climate Systems Lab. Lead Author for IPCC WGIII (Energy Systems), advisor to Chile's Ministry of Environment, and APEC consultant on hydrogen certification.
members.bio_long: Felipe Feijoo is an Associate Professor at the School of Industrial Engineering of Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso (PUCV), Chile. He directs the Energy & Climate Systems Lab and works at the intersection of energy systems modeling, climate policy, and operations research, with an emphasis on deep-decarbonization pathways under uncertainty and the interactions among energy, water, land, and food systems. He serves as a Lead Author for IPCC Working Group III (Chapter on Energy Systems), as advisor to the Scientific Committee on Climate Change at the Ministry of Environment of Chile, and as APEC consultant on hydrogen certification. He is Subject Editor of the journal ENERGY (Q1, IF 9.4), Co-Chair for the Americas of the SDEWES Centre, and Chair of the PhD program in Industrial Engineering at PUCV. He held postdoctoral positions at the University of Zagreb, PNNL/JGCRI (US DOE), and Johns Hopkins/MIT, and earned his Ph.D. from the University of South Florida.
education: Ph.D., Industrial Engineering — University of South Florida, 2015

members.name: Monica Castañeda
members.title: Co-Director · Energy & Climate Systems Lab
members.bio_short: Co-Director of the Energy & Climate Systems Lab, working on energy transitions, system dynamics, and policy modeling for sustainable development.
members.bio_long: Prof. Monica Castañeda serves as Co-Director of the Energy & Climate Systems Lab at PUCV. Her research combines system-dynamics modeling, policy analysis, and applied energy economics to study transitions toward low-carbon energy systems. She co-supervises graduate students in the lab and contributes to projects on decarbonization pathways and energy planning for Latin America.

members.name: Francisco Flores
members.title: PhD Alumnus · Postdoctoral Researcher
members.affiliation: University of Zagreb · PhD from PUCV (2025)
members.thesis: Strategic Energy Transition Planning in Latin America: An Integrated Approach with Cross-Border Trade and Flexible Technologies.
members.thesis_summary: Developed integrated energy-transition planning frameworks for Latin America that endogenously represent cross-border electricity and hydrogen trade together with flexible technologies (storage, demand response, Power-to-X). Combines integrated-assessment modeling (GCAM) with high-resolution power-system models (PyPSA, H2RES) to quantify the role of regional integration and flexibility in deep-decarbonization pathways.
members.bio_short: Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Zagreb. PhD alumnus of the ECS Lab. Works on integrated energy and climate modelling for Latin America, combining IAMs, power-system optimization, and water-energy-land nexus analyses.
members.bio_long: Francisco Flores is a Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Zagreb and a PhD alumnus of the Energy & Climate Systems Lab at PUCV. His research develops and applies integrated modeling frameworks — coupling Integrated Assessment Models (GCAM, GCAM-LA) with high-resolution power-system optimization (PyPSA, H2RES) — to study deep-decarbonization pathways for Latin America. His work explicitly accounts for cross-border electricity and hydrogen trade, flexible technologies, and the feedbacks among energy, water, and land systems. He has published in journals including Energy, Energy Strategy Reviews, and Applied Energy, and has collaborated with the U.S. Department of Energy / PNNL on the Net Zero World Initiative.
